adds.title: U.S. Department of State - Country Reports on Human Rights Practices for 2016 (Burundi)
adds.summary: In 2016 in Burundi consensual same-sex sexual activity was illegal under Article 567 of the penal code punishable by three months to two years imprisonment and a fine of 50,000 to 100,000 Burundian francs, no prosecutions were reported during the year, and LGBT persons faced societal discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity without government protection from such discrimination.

adds.title: International Gay and Lesbian Human Rights Commission - Burundi information
adds.summary: As of March 2026, Burundi allows no legal gender recognition and criminalizes same-sex relations under Article 250 of the Penal Code with up to two years in prison and fines, and LGBTIQ organizations cannot register; LGBTIQ people face high levels of harassment, discrimination, family rejection and stigmatization amid extrajudicial killings, enforced disappearances, arbitrary arrests, torture and sexual and gender-based violence with no meaningful legal reform, as shown by the March 2023 arrest of 24 people on same-sex conduct charges leading to acquittal on that charge after one accused died in detention but seven convictions for inciting debauchery, and by President Evariste Ndayishimiye stating in December 2023 that gay people should be stoned to death.

adds.title: Statement by President Evariste Ndayishimiye - December 2023
adds.summary: In December 2023 President Évariste Ndayishimiye said homosexuals found in Burundi should be taken to stadiums and stoned and rejected aid conditioned on respecting LGBT rights, while homosexual sex is illegal punishable by up to two years in jail and in August 2023 seven people were sentenced to one to two years in prison for engaging in homosexual acts.

adds.title: Remuruka Center in Bujumbura (as referenced in 2016 State Dept report)
adds.summary: During 2016 in Burundi consensual same-sex sexual activity remained criminalized under Penal Code Article 567 punishable by three months to two years imprisonment and a fine of 50,000 to 100,000 Burundian francs, no prosecutions under that provision were reported, LGBT persons including on grounds of gender identity faced societal discrimination and stigma without anti-discrimination protection, and the Remuruka Center in Bujumbura provided emergency shelter to at-risk LGBT individuals.
